name: Vintage Coachbuilt Car
region: Britain, France and the United States
summary: The pre-war luxury car. A long bonnet on a bare chassis, with a body that a coachbuilder made to order in aluminium over wood. The cabin is leather, walnut and cloth.

philosophy.core_thesis: A fine car is two works. The maker builds the chassis. The coachbuilder makes the body and the cabin to the taste of one buyer.
design_principles: Make the bonnet 40 to 50 percent of the car length, with the radiator upright at its front.
Build the body on an ash frame and clad it in hand-beaten aluminium panels.
Keep the mudguards separate from the body, in a long sweep from each wheel.
Fit the cabin with burr walnut veneer on the dashboard and the door caps.
Trim the seats in hide, and the rear compartment in wool cloth or silk damask.
Chrome or nickel plate the lamps, the radiator and the bumpers, and keep the plate bright.
Paint in two tones, one for the body and one for the mudguards or the roof, with a coach line between.
anti_patterns: Mudguards that merge into the body
A mass-made body with no hand work

silhouette.shape: A long, narrow car with an upright radiator, a very long bonnet, separate, long curved mudguards and a compact cabin set well back.
silhouette.line: A strong horizontal line from the radiator to the cabin, a curved running board and a rear that tapers or ends in a spare wheel.
silhouette.fit: The cabin sits behind the rear axle line of the engine; the occupants sit low, in an upright formal posture.
silhouette.proportion: Bonnet length 40 to 50 percent of the car; wheelbase 3.3 to 4.3 m; body height about 1.7 m.
rules: Set the driver far back, behind a long bonnet and a flat scuttle.
Run a coach line along the waist and the bonnet in a second colour.
Mount big separate headlamps on the front mudguards or on a bar.
Hold the rear compartment for the passengers behind a glass partition in a limousine.

fabrics.rule: Use real materials in the cabin: hide, burr walnut, silk or wool cloth and plated metal, all made by hand to fit one car.

methods: ash frame cut to a full-size drawing
aluminium panels beaten over a wood buck
burr walnut veneer matched in pairs
nickel and chrome plating of the brightwork
many coats of hand-rubbed cellulose paint
construction.closures: Doors hinged at the rear edge; plated handles; a folding hood with a plated frame on a tourer.
construction.details: A radiator mascot, a pair of big lamps and a luggage trunk at the rear. A silk blind covers the back window. The dashboard panel is engine-turned.

surface.pattern: Two-tone paint and a fine coach line; engine-turned metal and walnut grain in the cabin.
surface.gloss: Hand-rubbed paint at 80–95 GU; polished walnut at 60–80 GU; plated metal above 90 GU.
surface.wear: Leather and walnut gain a patina that owners value; plated metal is re-plated, not left to pit.

palette.strategy: Deep, sober body colours in two tones, a bright plated front and a cabin in the brown of hide and walnut.

processes: bespoke coachbuilding to a client order
making.scale: A chassis from the maker, a body from a coachbuilder; some makers build 1 to 3 bodies a week, and a one-off takes months.
making.signs: Panels with a hand-beaten line, matched walnut veneer, hand-sewn hide and a coachbuilder's plate on the sill.

pieces.form: Long-bonnet limousine with a glass partition and a formal rear compartment
Open two-seat body with a long bonnet and swept mudguards
Burr walnut panel with engine-turned instruments
Hand-sewn hide front seats and a rear compartment in fine cloth
Plated radiator shell, lamps and mascot
Thin wheel with a walnut rim and plated spokes

evidence.title: 1927 Rolls Royce Phantom I Limousine - Coachwork by Windovers.jpg

emotion.target_response: A sense of rank and calm: the viewer sees long lines, deep colour and hand work that only a rich owner could order.

use_cases: a period film about the 1920s and 1930s
an image prompt for a pre-war luxury car
a luxury brand story with a heritage car
avoid_when: the brief wants a mass-made small car
the brief wants speed and a smooth, closed body
the brief wants a plain modern cabin

modifiers.how: Merge the mudguards into the body, slope the tail and the radiator, and hide the lamps in the wings.
Shorten the bonnet, raise the body, and use wood wheels and brass lamps.

ornament_level.note: The mascot, the coach line and the engine-turned panel give a rich but formal look.
